reason: French 'ramilles' means twigs or small branches. PO branch has 'twig' and 'branchlet' as synonyms.
Latin 'ramulus' means a small branch or twig, which PO branch covers.
'ramuli' is the plural of ramulus, a small branch or twig.

A veinule is a small vein, and PO leaf lamina vein fits when the part is a leaf. The word is also used for veinlets in sepals, petals and bracts, where the leaf lamina vein class is wrong. PO lists 'veinlet' as a synonym of secondary leaf vein, so the finest order is not certain either.
Same as R3254: a plural veinule is only a leaf lamina vein when the bearer is a leaf. Outside leaves it needs a different vein class.
'abscission layer' is already a synonym of PO abscission zone.

Culm leaves are the sheathing, often bladeless leaves on bamboo and grass culms, and they differ from ordinary cauline leaves. Mapping them to cauline leaf loses the culm-sheath meaning and the culm context, and 'culm leave' looks like a typo. Prefer the leaf class with the culm as container, or reject.
Same as R3257: 'culm leaf' is a specific sheath-like leaf of bamboo, not any cauline leaf. Use leaf with container culm instead.
Same as R3257: plural of culm leaf, which is more specific than cauline leaf.

A sinker is a specialised root, such as a descending parasitic or haustorial root, or a water-seeking root. PO root is too general. A bare 'sinker' can also mean a fishing weight or a fruit-tree shoot, so the word is ambiguous. Reject, or use a sinker-root class if one is created.
A sinker root is a specific root type, usually a vertical root descending from a horizontal root. Mapping it to plain root loses that meaning. A constraint on the container would not fix it.
Same as R3261: plural of sinker root, which is a specific kind of root.
Same as R3260: 'sinkers' is ambiguous. In a plant context it means descending special roots, which plain PO root does not capture.
Ovary wall is the plain label of PO plant ovary wall.
'paroi de l'ovaire' is the French for ovary wall.

Bole is already a PO stem synonym and means the trunk of a tree. It is correct for trees and shrubs. It is wrong in the sense of a bole of a leaf bundle or a fungus-related use, and should not match other parts.

A resin dot is a resin-filled gland or secretory cavity visible on the surface, and mapping it to 'portion of secretory tissue' loses the resin and the dot shape. PO lists 'gland' as a synonym of this class, so a resin-dot mapping is a stretch. Prefer a gland class, or reject.
Same as R3267: a resin dot is a resin gland, not secretory tissue in general.
Same as R3267: the spaced form of resin-dot.

A panicled cyme is a cyme arranged in a panicle, so it has both a cyme and a panicle part. PO cyme inflorescence loses the panicle arrangement, which is a quality of the inflorescence. Better to map to cyme inflorescence with an arrangement quality, or leave it as a rule that adds the quality.
Same as R3270: 'paniculate cyme' loses the panicle arrangement.

A sporangiophore is a stalk that bears sporangia (in Equisetum, fungi). It is not a sporophyll, which is a leaf that bears sporangia. In Equisetum the sporangiophores are peltate scales, so they are not leaf-like in the PO sense. Reject, or ask for a new class.
Same as R3272: plural of sporangiophore, which is not a sporophyll.
'cormlet' is already a synonym for corm in PO (cormel). It is a small corm.
'cormel' is already a PO corm synonym.

A craspedium is the loment-like fruit of Mimosoideae (e.g. Entada) whose segments break away and leave the persistent frame (replum). It is a kind of loment. The match to loment fruit is close, though not perfect.
Plural of craspedium, with the same reasoning as R3276.

'secondary venation' means the pattern of secondary veins, which is a quality-like property of the leaf, not one organ. Mapping it to the secondary leaf vein class is a partial match. The venation pattern should be treated as a leaf quality, not a bearer.

Costal veins are veins along the leaf margin or the main rib, as in grasses and palms. They are not the same as secondary veins. In some floras 'costal' secondary veins arise from the midrib, but this is not reliable.
Same as R3279: plural of costal vein, which is not the same as secondary vein.

PO second order inflorescence axis has 'first order inflorescence branch' as a synonym, so it works for inflorescences. In other contexts a first-order branch is just a branch on a tree or shoot, where PO branch is right.
Same as R3281: plural form, and only correct when the part belongs to an inflorescence.

A fruiting head is a head-like fruit cluster, for example in Asteraceae. PO infructescence is the right class, but it loses the head form, which is a shape quality. Marginal: acceptable as a bearer if the shape is not required.
Same as R3283: 'fruit head' is an infructescence of head form.
Same as R3283: plural of fruiting head.

An anterior lip is the lower lip in a two-lipped corolla, so it fits the corolla lip when the whole is a corolla. A bare 'anterior lip' could also be a calyx lip or an orchid labellum. The class should be used only for corollas.
A lower lip is the anterior lip of a corolla, but 'lower lip' is also used for the calyx in Lamiaceae and for the orchid labellum. It is correct only when the whole is the corolla.

'with palea' is a phrase meaning 'has a palea', not a name for the part. It looks like a presence statement and should become an entity-presence rule on palea. Also, PO_0009038 is labelled palea but the lexicon lists palea as a synonym of inflorescence bract PO_0009054, so check the ID.

Floral scales in Cyperaceae and in conifers are bract-like structures, but in other plants 'floral scale' can be a perianth scale, such as the lodicule or a tepal-like scale in Juncaceae. Mapping every use to inflorescence bract loses that. Use only when the part is a spikelet or cone.
Same as R3289: plural of floral scale.
Oil tubes are the vittae of Apiaceae fruits, so the vitta class fits.
Spaced form of oil-tube, which is a vitta.
Plural of oil-tube, which is a vitta.
A staminal disc is a nectary disc around or inside the stamens. A synandrium is a fusion of stamens, so it is a different thing. Reject, or use a nectary disc class.
Same as R3294: an androecial disc is a disc-like structure of the androecium, not a synandrium.

A calycophyll is a petaloid, enlarged calyx lobe, as in Mussaenda. It is a particular type of calyx lobe, so mapping it to a plain calyx lobe loses the enlarged, leaf-like form. Possibly acceptable only with a quality added.
'enlarged calyx lobe' includes a size quality (enlarged). Mapping it to calyx lobe alone drops the enlarged meaning. It should be calyx lobe plus a size quality.

PO vascular bundle has 'vein' as a synonym, so strand fits when the part is a vascular bundle. 'Vascular strand' can also mean a single xylem or phloem strand, or a fibre strand, so it is not always a whole bundle.
Same as R3298: plural of vascular strand.

A chalk gland is a gland that secretes calcium carbonate (lime scales), as in Saxifraga. It is a type of hydathode in some cases, but not all hydathodes secrete chalk. Mapping it to hydathode loses the chalk-secretion meaning, though the match is plausible.
